newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SIIMANN IN FINAL TALKS ON NEW GOVT.
newsitem.headline: SIIMANN IN FINAL TALKS ON NEW GOVT.

text.p: Estonia's prime ministerial candidate Mart Siimann was on Friday in final negotiations over the make-up of the new government, a government spokesman said.
If settled, the proposed government could be presented to the president today.
"Negotiations are continuing," spokesman Juhan Kivirahk told Reuters.
Siimann was on Wednesday given the authority by parliament to form a new government within seven days and present it to President Lennart Meri.
The president then has three days to appoint Siimann prine minister and appoint his 14 ministers.
No major changes are expected in the government.
However Education Minister Rein Loik has resigned for personal reasons and the position of Agriculture Minister is under question.

Previous Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi stepped down last month after narrowly surviving a vote of no confidence amid allegations that he took part in shady privisation deals involving real estate in central Tallinn.
Siimann, a former television and radio station manager, has pledged to continue on the previous government's path of reforms.
